summary: Jan Christian Schaffert works in Indology and computational fields. Attested in 2026, he studied and served as a project collaborator (Mitarbeiter) on the EdiKILex project at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Jan Dolensky specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2013, he earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, where he studied under Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Jan E. M. Houben is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held posts at the Dutch Research Council (attested 1999) and Leiden University (attested 2000–2002) before becoming a directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2003.

Jan Fontein was an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Leiden University under Theodoor Paul Galestin. He served at the Rijksmuseum (1947–1955), as curator at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1966–1992), and at the Royal Ontario Museum (1990–1996).

Jan Gonda was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leiden and Utrecht universities under Willem Caland and Anton Gerard van Hamel. He held the Chair of Sanskrit (1929) and taught Indology (1932–1976) at Utrecht University.

Jan Hanusz was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Leipzig and completed his habilitation at Vienna under Georg Bühler and Friedrich Müller. He taught at the University of Vienna from around 1885 until 1887.

Jan Jakob Maria de Groot was a sinologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Leiden University and under Georg von der Gabelentz. He served as a professor at Leiden University (1891–1912) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1912–1921).

Jan Jaworski worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Warsaw under Stanisław Schayer and in Paris under Jean Przyluski, becoming a Privatdozent at the University of Warsaw in 1930.

Jan Jetso Boeles was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (1940–1945) under Nicolaas Johannes Krom and F. B. J. Kuiper, later serving as director of the Siam Society.

Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak was a sinologist who completed his doctorate at Leiden University and studied under Édouard Chavannes and Henri Cordier. He served as professor of Chinese language and literature at Leiden (1919; 1930–1954) and held visiting professorships at Columbia, Princeton, and Oxford.
Jan Kornelis de Cock was an Indologist. He completed his PhD at the University of Amsterdam in 1899, studying under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck.

Jan Laurens Andries Brandes worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern in 1884, subsequently serving as keeper at the National Museum of Indonesia (~1884–1905).

Jan Michał Rozwadowski was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Jagiellonian University and studied at Leipzig under Karl Brugmann and August Leskien. He served at Jagiellonian University from 1897, becoming professor and department head in 1904.

Jan Mrázek works in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He completed his doctoral studies under Josef Zubatý and became an associate professor at the National University of Singapore (attested 2011).

Jan N. Bremmer is a religious studies and history scholar who earned PhDs from the University of Amsterdam and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. He held posts at Utrecht University (1974–1990) and the University of Groningen (1990; 1996–2005).

Jan Nattier is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who earned her PhD from Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi. She held professorships at Macalester College, Stanford University, Indiana University Bloomington (1992–2005), and Soka University (2004–2010).

Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay was a linguist who earned his PhD at Leipzig and studied under August Leskien and August Schleicher. He held professorships at Kazan, Tartu, Jagiellonian University, Saint Petersburg State University, and the University of Warsaw.

Jan P. Hogendijk is a historian and Indologist who earned his doctorate from Utrecht University in 1983. He held professorships at Utrecht University (1986; 2005–2020) and Leiden University (2004–2009), with additional posts in Frankfurt, Tehran, and Saudi Arabia.

Jan Peter F. Hintelmann specializes in Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Marianne Pieper, and studied with traditional teachers including Thupten Nyandak, Tenzin Kunga, Sonam Senge, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.

Jan Rypka was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics who studied at the University of Vienna (~1905–1910). He held long-term posts at Charles University and its Faculty of Arts (~1925–1960), as well as the University of Paris.
